scope: Publicly documented Palantir AI FDE, Palantir MCP, and Pilot behavior compared with Foundry-lite product evidence. This does not claim access to Palantir proprietary implementation details.

statusDefinitions.current: A user-reachable product path has code, API or SDK surface, durable evidence, focused tests, and an explicit safety boundary.
statusDefinitions.partial: A bounded subset is implemented and the missing boundary is explicit.
statusDefinitions.future_gap: Not implemented as a user-reachable product capability.

axes.palantirContract: Natural-language intent is translated into governed native platform operations with contextual explanations.
axes.boundary: All execution uses native service contracts; the model cannot submit arbitrary tools or bypass platform permissions.

axes.palantirContract: A selected mode loads the relevant documentation, capabilities, and tools.
axes.boundary: Exploration, Ontology, data integration, data connection, Functions, governance, ML, OSDK React, and platform Q&A are permission-scoped current modes.

axes.palantirContract: The agent operates as the current user and remains inside normal permission and audit boundaries.
axes.boundary: The catalog hides unavailable tools and every execution rechecks the invoking principal's normal permission.

axes.palantirContract: Sessions start with minimal context and users can attach precise resources as needed.
axes.boundary: Dataset, Ontology/Pipeline branch, Source, Function, OSDK app, Project, Resource, and Model attachments are permission-checked, version-pinned, bounded, and recorded.

axes.palantirContract: Only configured native tools are exposed to the model.
axes.boundary: The server owns schemas, effects, confirmation policy, permissions, scope prefixes, and output limits. There are 69 server-owned tools: 43 exact-name tools from Palantir's public 72-tool catalog are wired to real Compass, Dataset, lineage, Ontology branch, Object Query, OSDK/Platform SDK, Developer Console, governed Data Connection, and documentation services; 26 are Foundry-lite-specific branch/test/proposal/Pilot tools. A catalog-derived integration ratchet executes all 69 through real Builder MCP JSON-RPC and checks one succeeded durable tool row per call. The remaining official 29 are not advertised until their underlying Code Repository, Global Branching, Compute Module, Dataset build/SQL, Developer Console conversion, or versioned webhook-update product foundation exists.

axes.palantirContract: Mutating tools require explicit user confirmation while read-only tools can run without confirmation.
axes.boundary: Each Builder MCP mutation first returns a fingerprint-bound challenge. A separate strict-OIDC human control-plane principal approves it, and the matching call can consume the short-lived confirmationReceipt exactly once from its outer JSON-RPC arguments; reusable environment or header confirmation is not accepted.

axes.palantirContract: Generated resource changes are isolated on a branch instead of directly editing production.
axes.boundary: Ontology and Pipeline authoring tools can modify only the selected branch; production activation and deployment are absent from the AI tool catalog.

axes.palantirContract: Branch changes move through proposal review before reaching the default branch.
axes.boundary: AI FDE may submit a proposal but cannot approve, execute, merge, deploy, or activate it.

axes.palantirContract: The agent executes tools, observes results, and iteratively adjusts until the task is complete.
axes.boundary: One turn supports one to eight durable tool steps, bounded outputs, and at most one consumption of each write confirmation.

axes.palantirContract: Sessions and tool activity remain attributable and auditable.
axes.boundary: Every model/tool/event/result is durable. After transport admission, a matching JSON-RPC retransmission returns the original Builder MCP success or business-error result without consuming tool quota again; an exhausted endpoint quota can first return HTTP 429 with Retry-After.

axes.palantirContract: The agent previews changes and uses validation or CI evidence before proposing them.
axes.boundary: Ontology migration evidence and Pipeline validation are returned before human proposal review. pipeline.branch.run_tests is explicitly static persisted-graph/output-contract proof with isDataExecution=false; it is not row execution or an output Dataset commit.

axes.palantirContract: Large tool catalogs can be searched and loaded lazily to reduce context use.
axes.boundary: AI FDE and external Builder MCP lazy modes start with search_tools, activate only app-scoped server-catalog matches, persist activation per session, emit tools/list_changed, isolate new sessions, and preserve eager fallback.

axes.palantirContract: The agent can expose a plan and ask structured clarifying questions before acting.
axes.boundary: Plans and clarifications are first-class structured tool results, persisted in the tool ledger and returned to the UI.

axes.palantirContract: Data, connections, functions, governance, ML, OSDK React, exploration, and platform Q&A have specialized modes.
axes.boundary: Each mode has explicit scope prefixes, capabilities, native adapters, and permission-filtered tool contracts.

axes.palantirContract: A builder-oriented MCP exposes governed resource-authoring tools separately from consumer Ontology MCP.
axes.boundary: MCP Streamable HTTP uses Authorization Code with PKCE, an exact Builder resource audience, app/client/resource-scope intersection, Origin checks, strict lifecycle and typed JSON-RPC IDs, canonical structured/text results, durable session-scoped lazy discovery, a single SSE lease with resume/termination, durable endpoint/tool admission, and fingerprint-bound one-time human confirmation receipts, with no approval/merge/deploy tools exposed on the Builder plane. The catalog-derived integration ratchet executes 49 reads and 20 separately confirmed mutations through JSON-RPC tools/call; the official Python ClientSession live gate keeps one session across branch reads and five confirmed writes against a separate strict-OIDC Uvicorn process and PostgreSQL. The current native breadth is 43 exact-name tools out of the official 72; the other 26 catalog entries are product-specific rather than false parity claims. Hosted ChatGPT SaaS and external IdP/DCR interoperability remain outside current live evidence.

axes.palantirContract: Natural language can generate an Ontology design, seed data, a React application, CI evidence, and a hosted application path.
axes.boundary: Generation creates replay-safe seed data, an isolated Ontology branch, restricted OSDK app, OSDK-backed React source, CI contract, durable resource, and a stable preview path; production use still requires human Ontology activation.
